content.title: About
content.content: Fuzzy Navel is a cocktail made with peach schnapps and orange juice. It is light, sweet, and fruit‑forward, typically served over ice in a tall glass. The name comes from the “fuzzy” peach flavor and the “navel” orange juice, which gives the drink its bright orange hue.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink first appeared in the United States in the 1980s when peach schnapps became widely available.
“Fuzzy” refers to the soft, peachy taste, while “Navel” denotes the orange juice from navel oranges.
It is often considered a “starter” cocktail for beginners because of its relatively low alcohol content (about 10‑12%).
A variation called “Hairy Navel” swaps peach schnapps for a creamy liqueur such as Baileys.
Bars sometimes serve Fuzzy Navel as a punch, adding soda water or lemonade for a lighter version.

items.title: Vitamin C from orange juice
items.content: Orange juice is rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Lower calorie count than many strong cocktails
items.content: When consumed in moderation, Fuzzy Navel contains fewer calories than cocktails based on high‑proof spirits.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The large volume of juice and ice helps maintain hydration, especially in warm weather.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Despite its mild strength, the drink still contains alcohol and can impair judgment and coordination.

items.title: Sugar in juice and schnapps
items.content: High sugar levels may be a concern for people with diabetes or those watching their weight.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to oranges should avoid this cocktail.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Pour 1½ oz peach schnapps into a glass filled with ice, add 4‑5 oz fresh orange juice, and stir gently. Garnish with an orange slice or a cherry if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Peach schnapps should be kept in a cool, dark place with the bottle tightly sealed. Orange juice is best stored in the refrigerator and used within 2‑3 days after opening.
